prerequisites: Having studied Physics in 2nd year of Bachillerato (Spanish high school)
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, which enable the student to learn new methods and technologies, as well as provide great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of their activity.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, studies, reports and task planning.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of fields, waves and electromagnetism and their application to solve engineering problems.
Understand the concept of a wave and know both its mathematical characterization and basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and put into practice problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Electric charge. Coulomb's Law. Electrostatic field and potential. Charge distributions. Electric dipole. Gauss's Law. Conductors. Capacitors. Electric field energy. Dielectrics.
Current intensity and density. Ohm's Law. Resistance. Joule effect. Generators: Electromotive force. DC circuits.

Magnetic field. Lorentz's Law: Magnetic induction. Hall effect. Magnetic force on an electric current. Magnetic field moment on a loop. Biot-Savart Law. Force between currents. Ampere's Theorem. Magnetic field energy. Magnetism in matter.
Electromagnetic induction: Faraday-Henry Law. Self-induction. Maxwell's Equations. RLC circuits. Electrical oscillations.
Free oscillations. Damped oscillations. Forced oscillations.
Concept of wave. Wave differential equation. Classification of waves. Harmonic waves. Mechanical waves. Wave phenomena. Sound waves. Doppler effect.
teaching_methods: Expositive classes (presentation and explanation of theoretical content and problem solving)
Classroom practices / seminars (problem solving, group work, presentation and defense of problems/projects)
Laboratory practices (handling measurement equipment, using simulation/data treatment software, analyzing results, preparing reports)
Individual or group problem-solving and report preparation
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, if minimums for P1 and P2 are met, Theory = (0.35 x P1) + (0.40 x P2) + (0.10 x PA). If P1 minimum is not met, Theory = (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA). Practices = (0.08 x P1) + (0.07 x P2) if practical block minimums are met. The final grade is (Theory) + (Practices) if theory minimums are met and 75% lab attendance is achieved, otherwise the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, Theory = (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA) with a minimum of 4 on ET. If attendance to practical classes was less than 75%, Practices = (0.15 x P2) with a minimum of 4 on P2. Differentiated evaluation follows extraordinary call criteria.
